item.title: Rebar - Wikipedia
item.description: Rebar (short for reinforcement bar or reinforcing bar), known when massed as reinforcing steel or steel reinforcement, [1] is a tension device added to concrete to form reinforced concrete and reinforced masonry structures to strengthen and aid the concrete under tension.

item.title: 1/2" x 20' Rebar Grade 60 (#4) at Menards®
item.description: Rebar or Reinforcing bar is a ribbed steel bar that is used in concrete slabs or in structures to strengthen a building. Rebar is used inside of concrete to strengthen a building, sidewalk, patio or even roads. Rebar has multiple uses and can be installed in horizontal or vertical applications.

item.title: What is rebar: types, uses, and a complete guide for beginners
item.description: Rebar is a deformed steel bar embedded in concrete to add tensile strength that concrete alone cannot provide. The word is short for "reinforcing bar," and it has been the defining material of modern construction for well over a century.
